messages:
maya: paging oncall, seeing a weird spike to auth service from a handful of IPs, looks like repeated token reuse requests. many are 401 -> 200 after retries. tagging @oncall 

jonah: deploying a honeypot rule now to drop replayed tokens. can someone grab a pcap or request dump? :eyes: 

kate-sre: I have logs. adding a short sample to thread. suspicious pattern: repeated Authorization: Bearer <token> with same jti across different client_ids.

maya: pasting obfuscated sample (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T02:01:12Z] src=3.8.12.44 auth_proxy requestId=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=401 token_jti=abcd-ef01 client_id=svc-analytics
[2026-03-15T02:01:13Z] src=3.8.12.44 auth_proxy requestId=abc124 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 token_jti=abcd-ef01 client_id=svc-frontend
```

jonah: looks like token replay across clients. could be leaked debug logs with tokens in them. check S3 buckets for recent uploads with debug level.

sec-eng: Confirmed. we see s3://redwood-staging-logs/debug/2026-03-15/ had a file with stack traces that contained Bearer tokens. ACLs look private but suspect credential exposure.

incident-bot: Incident P1 created: suspicious-auth-replay (auto-assigned: @oncall). Pagerduty alert sent.

ryan-support: any customer impact yet? do we have live errors or escalations?

maya: customer-facing API rate limiting briefly triggered; some customers saw 401 then succeeded — may have caused some confusion but still serving. no data leak to external user data plane yet that we can confirm.

kate-sre: mitigation plan I'm pushing now: 1) disable auth-proxy token acceptance for old jti reuse (hotfix toggle), 2) rotate service tokens for affected downstream services, 3) rotate leaked tokens, 4) reingest/scan S3 for other leaked files.

jonah: hotfix is ready, rolling a toggle via consul: `curl -X POST https://consul/api/kv/feature/auth-token-reuse-block -d true` then reload auth-proxy.

deploy-bot: Started rollout: auth-proxy v1.9.2-hotfix -> canary on us-west-2 (10% traffic). logs: https://deploys/redwood/rollouts/2765432100

maya: start key rotation scripts? I can run rotate for cached tokens: `./scripts/rotate_service_keys.sh --pattern leaked-* --parallel 4`

sec-eng: hold on — we need to identify token issuers first. rotating blindly will break customers. do a staged rotate: affected service tokens first, then user tokens via forced session invalidation.

ryan-support: drafting support note for affected customers, suggest asking impacted teams to rotate any long-lived service tokens and check audit logs. will post stubs once we confirm scope.

maya: ops-bot, can you snapshot current session store and backup before invalidation?

ops-bot: Snapshot started: sessions-db backup id=sb-2765432100, ETA 2m.

kate-sre: legal — any compliance notifications? potential PII exposure if tokens permitted data exfil.

legal: thanks. please tag me with affected customer list as soon as available. we might need to trigger breach-notice playbook. keep any raw tokens offline and do not paste into public channels.

jonah: I scanned recent object uploads in production buckets with `aws s3api list-objects` and grepped for "Bearer ". Found 3 objects in s3://ingest-logs/debug/2026-03-15/ that contain tokens. marking paths.

sec-eng: good catch. mark those objects as evidence and move to secure bucket: `aws s3 mv s3://ingest-logs/debug/2026-03-15/obj123 s3://sec-evidence/2765432100/ --acl private` then run `aws s3api put-object-tagging` to tag as "evidence=true".

maya: executing evidence move now.

maya: moved object obj123, obj127, obj129 -> sec-evidence/2765432100. hashes: md5s match.

jonah: auth-proxy canary reports reduced replay hits by ~95% after toggle. no further 200 after 401 for seen JTIs.

deploy-bot: Canary success. Proceeding rollout to 50% in 30s.

ryan-support: creating a short customer advisory draft: "We detected suspicious token reuse patterns originating from leaked debug logs. We're rotating impacted tokens and invalidating sessions. If you manage long-lived service tokens, rotate them and follow the steps in our KB: https://help.redwood/rotate-tokens" — will paste full text for approval.

sec-eng: checklist/status: evidence secured (3 files), hotfix deployed canary -> 10% -> 50%, key rotation plan ready but staged, session invalidation paused until support comms go out, legal engaged.

kate-sre: next steps: 1) complete rollout, 2) rotate service tokens for svc-analytics and svc-frontend, 3) force short TTL for all sessions for 24h (2m rolling restart to evict), 4) postmortem scheduler.

maya: I'm rotating svc-frontend token now, running script in dry-run first then live. `./scripts/rotate_service_keys.sh svc-frontend --dry-run`

jonah: dry-run output looks good. are we ready to trigger live rotate?

legal: recommend notifying customers with elevated risk after rotation begins, include remediation steps. avoid language that implies unauthorized access to customer data unless we confirm.

ryan-support: approved wording from legal. posting advisory to status page in 5m.

maya: started live rotate svc-frontend -> new key issued 3m ago, updating auth-service trust store.

ops-bot: sessions-db backup complete sb-2765432100 available at s3://backups/sessions/sb-2765432100.tar.gz

jonah: rolling TTL change: updating env var SESSION_MAX_AGE=3600 and issuing rolling restart for session svc (1% at a time).

sec-eng: monitoring metrics: token-reuse hits trending down to normal baseline. 5xx unchanged. customer error rate for auth spiked by 0.7% during rotate window.

ryan-support: status page posted: https://status.redwood/incidents/2765432100. customers notified with recommended steps.

maya: final checklist: finish rotating remaining affected service tokens, keep hotfix toggle enforced for 24h, schedule postmortem, prepare CISA if required.

jonah: tagging this as handled for now, keeping channel open for postmortem and any followups. great work everyone. :clap: 

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> status: mitigated. timeline: hotfix deployed, evidence secured, tokens rotated, customer notifications posted.

legal: keep all evidence retention flags for 1 year. continue to update privacy team if anything new shows up.

kate-sre: postmortem owner assigned: jonah. ETA draft: 72h.

maya: thanks team. closing but will re-open if any regressions.
